requirements.requirement: Enable a persistent host firewall on node1.
requirements.summary: firewalld was active and enabled before restart, its permanent configuration validated successfully, and it recovered active and enabled under a different boot identity with the same runtime and permanent policy.

requirements.requirement: Permit inbound SSH and TCP port 8080 while rejecting unrelated inbound connections.
requirements.summary: Runtime and permanent policy allow SSH and 8080/tcp. Direct tests before and after restart accepted ports 22 and 8080 while rejecting unrelated TCP ports 9090 and 18080. The former Cockpit allowance was removed.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the platform.
requirements.summary: RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0 remained unchanged across execution and restart. The implementation used the already-installed RHEL-packaged firewalld 2.3.0 and nftables 1.1.1 stack, with no package installation or kernel change shown.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The firewall policy was directly tested before and after a verified restart, and the provider-wide restart protocol is complete for node1: healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered services and policy are all captured. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the restart.
limitations: Behavioral rejection testing was bounded to IPv4 TCP ports 9090 and 18080; IPv6 and unrelated UDP traffic were supported by policy inspection rather than equivalent direct connection tests.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The temporary namespaces, veth interfaces, listeners, files, and runtime interface assignments used for bounded baseline and final behavior tests had direct evidentiary purposes and were removed by their cleanup handlers. Permanent mutations were limited to adding 8080/tcp and removing the unrelated Cockpit allowance; reload and restart activated and verified persistence. Final checks found no test residue, failed units, damaged package state, or unexpected listeners.
